newsitem.title: UK: First fall in BFI since late September.
newsitem.headline: First fall in BFI since late September.

text.p: The Baltic Freight index was reduced by one point on Thursday to 1,521 points, its first fall since Sept 25 when it stood at 992.
Brokers said that although Atlantic Caper rates were rising the chief reason for the fall in the BFI was weaker Panamax grain rates from the USGulf to China and Japan.

Dreyfus were believed to have fixed 52,000 heavy grain end-November USGulf to Japan at $25.25 basis no combination and possibly also $24.25 for early December if market rumours were correct. But there was some doubt about this level which may have been agreed some seven to 10 days ago.
Brokers were finding the future course of the market difficult to read, and opinion was divided about imminent prospects.
BIFFEX continued to fall as the lower Panamax grain rates circulated and by 1300 GMT was down 35 to 50 points in a turnover of 326 lots.
